A circle has circumference 88 cm. What is its radius (use π = 22/7)?
Explain why the area of a circle is πr², using the idea of cutting it into slices.
questions.modelAnswer: Cut the circle into many equal sector slices and arrange them alternately point-up and point-down. They form a shape close to a parallelogram (almost a rectangle). Its height is the radius r, and its length is half the circumference, πr. So the area is πr × r = πr². The more slices, the closer it gets to a rectangle.
